mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille convention member-state route: (1) notarisation in the country of origin; (2) Apostille certificate issued by the designated competent authority; (3) certified Simplified Chinese translation. Non-member-state parallel route: (1) notarisation; (2) authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the foreign state; (3) consular legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate General; (4) certified Chinese translation. The two routes are mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding each ultimate beneficial owner, director, authorised signatory and material counterparty, the compliance team must screen against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and all applicable PRC foreign sanctions and counter-terrorism lists published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Commerce. Individual and entity screening must be performed using a licensed commercial database supplemented by negative-news and adverse-media searches. Any politically exposed person, family member, close associate, or entity owned by such persons must receive enhanced due diligence, including written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, independent verification of beneficial ownership, escalation to the senior compliance committee, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse screening results must be resolved by a written compliance memorandum approved by the AML/CFT compliance officer and the responsible legal partner. All screening records must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Pre-clearance Portal, accessed through the provincial AMR online service platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of a PRC WFOE must be in Simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or activity descriptor, and the corporate form suffix limited liability company. The name cannot be wholly in pinyin, foreign-language script, Arabic numerals, or special symbols. A foreign trade name may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese characters that have no objectionable meaning and that do not mislead as to nature or scope of the enterprise. The foreign-language equivalent may be used outside the business licence but is not a registered name. The chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name in the same or closely related industry within the same administrative district, and must not contain any prohibited or sensitive token.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An approved name reservation may be extended once for another 30 days if the formation filing is submitted before the original expiry and the district AMR consents. Upon rejection, the applicant must first correct the grounds cited in the preliminary refusal notice and resubmit through the same portal. If the revised name is still rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the district AMR within 15 working days, attaching the rejection notice, the original and revised name charts, the entity structure, and a legal opinion. If the district AMR still refuses, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the municipal AMR or the local People's Government within 60 days, and thereafter may institute administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months. Each appeal must be submitted in Chinese through a duly authorised signatory.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a WFOE engaged in outsourced virtual CFO services. PRC company law and tax regulations require an actual business address shown on the business licence, used for service of process, tax registration, payroll, and invoice management. State Taxation Administration inspectors and commercial banks reject a bare virtual address because bank KYC and AML controls require physical verification of the operating premises and evidence of real business substance. A shared office or government-designated incubator seat providing a genuine workstation, meeting room, registered address, and documented lease may be accepted in some provinces; however, the authorities will still require a valid lease agreement, rental invoices, and an on-site manager. Therefore, any virtual office arrangement must be paired with a physical presence sufficient to pass verification by the AMR, tax authorities, and the opening bank.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection readiness checklist: (1) lease agreement and landlord identity certificate filed; (2) rental invoice records maintained; (3) business signage or employee presence at the registered address during normal working hours; (4) office equipment consistent with virtual CFO and bookkeeping services; (5) annual tax and statistical reports consistent with the declared scope of business; (6) a designated person available to meet inspectors. Quantified risk: there is an approximately 45% to 60% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax or AMR authorities within the first 12 months for a small-scale WFOE service enterprise, with the likelihood rising above 60% in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen if no visible office is maintained. Banks will also conduct a physical inspection before final approval of the corporate current account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), effective 1 July 2024, particularly Articles 23-37 (formation and registration), Article 47 (five-year capital contribution period for limited liability companies), Articles 58-68 (shareholders' powers and governance organs), and Article 93 (incorporation of wholly foreign-owned enterprises as limited liability companies); together with the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019) and the Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law; and the Measures for the Registration of Market Entities (2021).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Enterprise Registration, State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) at the company's intended registered address in China (Mainland).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company together with the Company's Articles of Association and the Notice of Pre-approval of Company Name.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to a general-purpose WFOE providing outsourcing, accounting, or virtual CFO advisory services under ISIC 6920. The registered capital amount is self-declared and must be reasonably consistent with the announced business scale. Under Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law, all shareholders must pay the full subscribed capital contribution within five years from the date of incorporation. There is no blocked escrow account requirement under PRC law; however, the foreign investor's capital contribution must be remitted through a licensed bank into a foreign exchange settlement capital account opened in the name of the WFOE and reported to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the FDI foreign exchange registration procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (THE COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING

WHEREAS the Company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise organized as a limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and WHEREAS the Board of Directors is authorized by the Articles of Association to take corporate formation actions on behalf of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION: The Articles of Association of CN_WFOE_LTD, as submitted for registration, are hereby approved, ratified, and adopted as the supreme internal governing instrument of the Company. The registered name, registered address, business scope, organizational structure, capital contribution rules, and governance procedures contained in the Articles are confirmed in all respects.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The sole foreign shareholder of the Company is hereby acknowledged as subscribing to one hundred percent of the registered capital of the Company. The legal representative and the chief financial officer are authorized to open a foreign exchange settlement account for the Company, receive the subscribed capital contribution, and cause such capital to be recorded in the Company's statutory books. All contributions shall be paid in full within the statutory five-year period, and no distribution or dividend may be made before the paid-in capital obligations are fulfilled in accordance with the Articles and applicable law.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be the address stated in the application for establishment registration. The legal representative is irrevocably authorized to execute the office lease, accept service of process, file all address-related amendments, and take all steps necessary to maintain the registered office in good standing.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall maintain banking relationships with licensed commercial banks in the People's Republic of China. The Chairman, the General Manager, the Chief Financial Officer, and the legal representative are each authorized, in such combinations as the banking mandates require, to open and operate the basic deposit account, foreign exchange settlement account, and any auxiliary accounts necessary for the Company's business. The board ratifies any banking forms, signature cards, mandates, and account agreements executed by or on behalf of the Company in connection with this authorization.

5. STATUTORY OFFICERS: The following officers are appointed with statutory effect: the Chairman and Legal Representative shall have the executive authority to represent the Company and sign all binding corporate documents; the General Manager shall supervise the daily operations of the Company; the Chief Financial Officer shall oversee bookkeeping, mult  icurrency ledgers, tax filings, and treasury management; and the Supervisor shall exercise independent audit and monitoring powers as required by law. Each officer shall act within the delegated authority and in accordance with the Articles of Association.

6. COMPANY SEALS: The Company shall cause the engraving of the official company seal, the financial seal, the legal representative seal, and the invoice seal through a Public Security Bureau-licensed engraving enterprise. The use of any seal shall be recorded in the Company's seal-use ledger.

7. ACCOUNTING AND FISCAL YEAR: The Company's financial books shall be maintained in RMB, on the accrual basis, under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises. The fiscal year shall begin on January 1 and end on December 31 of each calendar year. The Chief Financial Officer is authorized to select and contract with qualified licensed accountants and tax advisors as required.

8. RATIFICATION AND EFFECTIVENESS: All actions taken by the founders, attorneys, and agents in furtherance of the incorporation, registration, licensing, and operational setup of the Company prior to the date of this resolution are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved as acts of the Company. This resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by governmental authorities, banks, lessors, counterparties, and counsel until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Coding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform or the local AMR enterprise registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for pre-approval of the company name in Chinese, together with a declaration of intended business scope. The business scope must be coded and expressly include accounting advisory services, bookkeeping services, financial management consulting, virtual CFO services, tax consultation, and enterprise management services. Verify that the proposed scope is not listed in the negative list for foreign investment under the Special Administrative Measures for Access of Foreign Investment. Ensure the proposed name contains a distinct jurisdictional prefix plus industry segment and ends with Limited Liability Company. Obtain the official Name Pre-approval Notice before proceeding to incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Pre-approval of Company Name
Passport or corporate registration certificate of the foreign investor
Power of attorney authorizing the local formation agent
Proposed Chinese company name
Intended business scope description
Identity document of the proposed legal representative
Office lease intent letter or address declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity or prohibited elements, the applicant may resubmit with up to three alternative names; if the business scope contains negative-list wording, revise the scope and resubmit. An administrative appeal may be filed with the SAMR at the same level, or the application may be corrected within ten working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Enterprise Registration Department, local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) through the Government Services Center or the same-level online registration system under SAMR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal establishment registration application for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited by shares or limited liability, as elected in the Articles. The application must include all statutory appendices: the approved Articles of Association, the name pre-approval notice, the investor's notarized and legalized (apostilled) identity or corporate existence record, the lease agreement for the registered office, the landlord's property ownership certificate, and the appointment documents for the legal representative, directors, general manager, and supervisor. The filing officer will examine the capital contribution schedule, the governance structure, and the legality of the business scope. On approval, the AMR will issue the Unified Social Credit Code Business License in the name of CN_WFOE_LTD. The registration itself constitutes the formal tax registration through the five-in-one system.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Articles of Association executed by the sole foreign investor and all directors
Company Name Pre-approval Notice
Certificate of incorporation or passport of the foreign investor, notarized and apostilled or legalized as required
Office lease agreement and landlord property certificate
Consent and appointment of legal representative and director
Identity documents of legal representative, directors, general manager, supervisor
Power of attorney in favor of the formation agent or external counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a query or suspension notice, the applicant must respond in writing within fifteen working days by curing the flagged inconsistency, supplementing the missing notarization, or correcting the capital contribution schedule. If administrative rejection is suspected to be unlawful, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the SAMR or a higher-level Market Regulation Administration, or ultimately commence an administrative lawsuit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Logistics: Seals, Bank Accounts, and Office Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-licensed seal engraving enterprise; a licensed commercial bank in China for the Basic Deposit Account; and the local Fire and Rescue Department where the commercial landlord requires fire acceptance documentation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business License is obtained, the legal representative shall cause the engraving of the company official seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal, and contract seal at a licensed engraving enterprise authorized by the Public Security Bureau. Next, the Company shall open a RMB basic deposit account at a licensed commercial bank and, if foreign capital will be remitted, apply for a foreign exchange settlement capital account through the same bank. The bank will require a board resolution appointing account signatories, which is covered by the First Board Resolution. If the leased office is not fire-compliant, the Company shall coordinate with the landlord to ensure the premises hold a valid commercial fire safety acceptance certificate; a copy shall be retained in the corporate compliance file.
required_dossiers: Original Business License with Unified Social Credit Code
Legal representative identity document
Seal engraving approval and certificate of entrusted seal engraving enterprise
First Board Resolution establishing bank account authority
Completed bank account application forms and signatory mandates
Office lease agreement and landlord property certificate
Fire safety acceptance certificate for the commercial premises (if applicable or required by lease)
Tax registration information sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening application because of deficient signatory documentation, the Company shall correct the powers of attorney and banking mandate forms and resubmit. If the seal engraving enterprise reports a discrepancy in the registered name, the Company must contact the AMR to endorse the Business License correction. Fire non-compliance is curable by obtaining a landlord-provided fire safety inspection letter or by engaging a licensed fire engineering firm to perform rectification works before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Insurance, Foreign Investment Reporting, and SAFE FDI Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration (STA); local branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting through a qualified designated bank; and the Ministry of Commerce or delegated provincial commerce department through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although the Business License contains the unified tax identifier, the Company must complete ancillary tax activation in the electronic tax bureau, select the accounting software, add the digital electronic invoice scheme, and register for value-added tax as either general or small-scale taxpayer depending on projected revenue. The Company must also perform social insurance and housing fund registration for its employees before hiring staff. For foreign invested funds, the Company must complete the FDI foreign exchange registration through a designated bank using SAFE's Foreign Exchange Administration system; the remitted capital must be credited only to the foreign exchange settlement capital account. Concurrently, the Company must file its Foreign Investment Information Report with the Ministry of Commerce as mandated by the Foreign Investment Law, reporting basic investor information, capital contributions, and the ultimate beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: Business License of CN_WFOE_LTD
Articles of Association
Completed tax registration and digital invoice application forms
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms and employment records of initial staff
First Board Resolution authorizing bank account operations
FDI foreign exchange registration application form and bank mandate
Foreign investor identity documents
Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting Form and ultimate beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority suspends invoice quota approval, the Company may request a temporary invoice cap and later apply for permanent quota. If SAFE returns the FDI registration application, correct any mismatch between the capital contribution schedule in the Articles and the bank remittance instruction and resubmit through the designated bank; unresolved foreign exchange issues may be escalated to the local SAFE branch for guidance, and administrative review is available for procedural errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Agency Bookkeeping License for ISIC 6920 Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Finance Bureau of the local municipal government, specifically the Department of Accounting Affairs, through the National Agency Bookkeeping Management Electronic System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the WFOE will operate as an outsourced virtual CFO and agency bookkeeping service provider under ISIC 6920 and NAICS 541219, it must obtain the Agency Bookkeeping License under the Measures for Agency Bookkeeping issued by the Ministry of Finance. The Company must demonstrate that at least three full-time employees are qualified professional accountants, that the head of accounting possesses an accounting professional qualification, and that the Company has an internal quality control system governing client records, confidentiality, data security, multi-currency conversion, and ledger integrity. Submit the application with employment contracts, professional certificates, the internal operating manual, and office premise proof to the local Finance Bureau. Upon approval, the Company will be lawfully authorized to engage in commercial bookkeeping and financial management advisory services.
required_dossiers: Application Form for Agency Bookkeeping License
Business License of CN_WFOE_LTD
Employment contracts of at least three accounting professionals
Professional qualification certificates of accounting personnel
Proof of office premises and equipment
Internal quality control and client confidentiality system manual
Declaration of no material violation within the preceding three years
Power of attorney of the person filing the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Finance Bureau rejects the application, the Company may cure the stated deficiencies within ten working days and submit a new application. If the rejection is based on staff qualifications, the Company may add qualified accountants and resubmit. The Company may also request a written administrative reconsideration from the next higher finance authority if the denial is appealed on legal grounds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Finance Bureau of the local municipal government for the statutory Agency Bookkeeping License; no industrial authority applies because ISIC 6920 is an office-based professional services activity and does not constitute physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agency Bookkeeping License issued under the Measures for Agency Bookkeeping of the Ministry of Finance, together with the Business License containing the registered business scope for financial management consulting and accounting advisory services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau under the Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — the activity is pure digital/consulting in nature and does not involve production, assembly, chemical handling, manufacturing, or warehousing; therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment report, environmental registration, or EIA approval is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the operation generates no industrial wastewater, no VOCs, no hazardous waste, and no stationary combustion emissions. The office must, however, comply with municipal waste classification rules and may not co-locate with any manufacturing or chemical activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a special Civil Defense fire permit because no manufacturing or high-risk physical operation is present. The Company must nevertheless ensure the leased commercial premises have a valid fire safety acceptance certificate under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and must make a simple workplace safety registration with the local emergency management authority as an employer of office-based staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); official electronic filing portal is the National Electronic Tax Service Platform (e-Tax@China), accessible through www.chinatax.gov.cn, covering tax registration, VAT filing, invoice issuance, export tax refund/zero-rating applications, and corporate income tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), no separate Tax Identification Number application is required; the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code printed on the Business License issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) is the legal Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT registration number. The incorporation dossier is automatically transmitted from SAMR to the local STA office, completing tax registration on an ex officio basis. After incorporation, the legal representative and finance officer must activate the taxpayer account on the e-Tax@China portal using the registered mobile phone, real-name authentication, and electronic tax device authorization; they must then verify or update enterprise tax registration information, banking and capital account details, VAT payer type election, electronic invoice quotas, and applicable accounting/filing frequency. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that does not have a Chinese establishment but derives Chinese-source income, the non-resident entity or its withholding agent must apply for non-resident tax identification registration with the competent STA office for the location of the payer or place of income derivation, submitting the foreign enterprise registration certificate, board resolution or appointment document, contract or agreement, and beneficial ownership self-certification; the STA issues a non-resident tax registration record that is used for withholding tax, VAT, and stamp duty compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None, because China maintains a unitary corporate income tax system with no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections; however, for indirect tax purposes the WFOE may elect small-scale VAT taxpayer status at the inception of operations, or apply to become a General VAT Payer, and the General VAT Payer designation allows input VAT credit recovery and eligibility for export zero-rating.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) administered nationally under the People's Republic of China VAT system, with the headline goods rate at 13% and taxable modern services, including disclosed fiduciary and advisory services, at 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in taxable turnover measured over any trailing consecutive 12-month period is the mandatory threshold for registration as a General VAT Payer; all Chinese WFOEs are automatically tax-registered at incorporation, so no separate VAT entity registration threshold applies, but a taxpayer whose annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 must file a General VAT Payer registration with the STA and comply with special VAT invoice issuance, input VAT crediting, and monthly/quarterly filing rules, while the current small-scale taxpayer administrative exemption for turnover not exceeding RMB 100,000 per month may apply where the taxpayer has not elected General VAT Payer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the Fapiao VAT invoice system with real-time fiscal supervision through the STA electronic invoice platform. All VAT special invoices and ordinary invoices must be issued through the official e-Tax channel or STA-approved software/API endpoint, with each invoice carrying a unique digital monitoring code, a digital tax-control signature, and encrypted transaction data uploaded to the STA at issuance. The fully digitalized electronic invoice (FDEI) framework eliminates the need for physical pre-printed invoice stock and requires the seller to obtain an approved electronic invoice quota, maintain a synchronous invoice-data reconciliation file, and include the correct commodity or service classification code, VAT rate, buyer Unified Social Credit Code, and tax amount. Failure to clear invoice data through the STA anti-fraud digital control environment can render an invoice invalid for VAT deduction, for export refund purposes, or as a valid corporate expense voucher.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are eligible for 0% VAT zero-rating when the WFOE is a General VAT Payer, the goods have actually departed from China under a valid export customs declaration filed with the General Administration of Customs, the exporter retains the export sales contract and transport documents, and the export proceeds are received from an overseas buyer and repatriated through a Chinese bank. Cross-border services, including qualifying outsourced virtual CFO and bookkeeping/consulting services delivered to non-resident clients, may qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption when the service recipient is located outside China, the services are actually rendered outside China or consumed entirely offshore, the payment originates from abroad and is received in foreign currency, and the service falls within the STA cross-border taxable services guidance; full 0% zero-rating is specifically available for certain statutory offshore services such as technology/IT, software, R&D, and specified business process outsourcing, while other cross-border advisory services may be subject to VAT exemption rather than zero-rating unless the taxpayer obtains the relevant STA confirmation or administrative ruling.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (Export Bill of Entry) issued and electronically confirmed by the General Administration of Customs
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or International Consignment Note proving physical export movement from mainland China
Commercial invoice issued in the name of the overseas buyer and packing list describing the exported goods
Original or electronically authenticated export sales contract or purchase order with the offshore customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank-issued Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payments Transaction Certificate from a SAFE-designated Chinese bank proving receipt of export proceeds from abroad
Export rebate/zero-rating claim record generated in the e-Tax@China export tax system

For cross-border services: signed offshore service agreement, service delivery report, performance or completion certificate, evidence of the non-resident client's foreign tax residence, and bank SWIFT credit confirmation showing receipt of foreign-currency consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and General Administration of Customs jointly audit export zero-rating and VAT refund claims through documentary, logistics, payment-trail, and enterprise-accounting cross-checks. Any zero-rating or export refund claim not supported by the mandatory customs, transport, invoicing, and foreign-exchange repatriation documentation is reversed, with the output VAT recaptured at the applicable domestic rate, interest and late payment surcharges imposed, and a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Law on Tax Administration and Tax Collection. Where zero-rating is obtained by fabricating export declarations, false bills of lading, or fake remittance certificates, the taxpayer is additionally liable for confiscation of the wrongly refunded tax, customs penalties, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent export-tax refund under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which may result in imprisonment and severe fines; the responsible legal representative, financial officer, and any accomplice may also be subject to personal liability, travel restrictions, and market-entry prohibitions in aggravated egregious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), acting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China achieves current account convertibility under IMF Article VIII while maintaining a managed floating exchange rate subject to SAFE oversight. Operating revenues in RMB arising from exported CFO services can be converted and remitted through an authorized bank if supported by genuine commercial invoices and the bank's real-business-needs review. Inbound equity capital injections, however, are capital account transactions requiring FDI registration with SAFE or its delegated bank, payment into a designated foreign currency capital account, and use of converted RMB strictly in accordance with the Foreign Investment Negative List and the approved business scope. Profit remittances are current account investment income: the WFOE must submit audited financial statements, corporate income tax payment certificates, a shareholder distribution resolution, and historical audit evidence to the remitting bank, which then performs a documentary check and reports to SAFE. Export or service-export proceeds do not have a mandatory conversion percentage, but they must be repatriated to China within the statutory period and settled only through licensed banks at market rates. Capital account items such as cross-border loans, guarantees, foreign exchange derivatives, and overseas investment remain subject to quotas, filings, or case-by-case SAFE approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished blanket mandatory surrender requirements for foreign exchange export proceeds under the 2012 reform package. For goods trade, export proceeds must be repatriated to China within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration or the date the overseas collection right becomes due, subject to verification under SAFE's cross-border receipt and payment system. There is no fixed statutory conversion ratio; the exporter may retain proceeds in a current account foreign exchange settlement account or convert them to RMB at the prevailing market rate through an authorized domestic bank. For service exports such as outsourced CFO advisory fees, proceeds must be repatriated in accordance with the underlying service contract and reported to SAFE through the collecting bank using the appropriate balance-of-payments transaction code before any conversion or retention decision is executed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Operational Account and Current-Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Equity Injection and RMB Operational Account
Multicurrency Operational Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for any onshore clearing or account-keeping function. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise and Stripe are not licensed banks or qualified foreign-invested financial institutions in China and cannot maintain onshore RMB or foreign currency settlement accounts for a mainland WFOE. They may be used only as upstream payment acceptance or invoicing tools that route funds through an authorized domestic bank account; all SAFE reporting, FX conversion, and capital verification must remain with a licensed Chinese commercial bank. Fintech EMI balances cannot act as treasury liquidity in mainland China without a banking license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed WFOE, the legal representative and all authorized signatories must generally attend an in-branch KYC interview at account opening; pure remote opening is not available for the first account. Some banks permit a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, combined with a verified video call, to allow a local finance manager to be the account signatory when the foreign legal representative cannot travel. China's accession to the Apostille Convention on 7 November 2023 simplifies document legalization, but the underlying bank KYC policy and the PBOC's branch-level interview requirement remain decisive. In practice, Beijing and Shanghai international settlement departments are more flexible for foreign-owned entities than smaller provincial branches.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership chain passes through multiple holding entities, trusts, or opaque investment structures, triggering sanctions and PEP screening concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete ownership chart traced to natural persons, certified copies of registration documents for each intermediate entity, passport pages of all UBOs, signed political exposure declarations, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence including bank statements and tax returns, transaction-blockchain analysis of capital flows, and a formal legal opinion confirming no sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The virtual CFO service model has a light physical footprint and potentially high transaction velocity, which may be mischaracterized as invoice fabrication or shell-trading activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A substantive office lease or property ownership certificate, payroll and social insurance records for resident employees, client engagement letters, detailed statements of work, milestone-based deliverables, time-tracking and project management logs, management accounts, an internal controls manual, and a transfer pricing documentation package substantiating arm's-length pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound foreign currency capital contribution requires special capital account verification; incorrect use or premature conversion to RMB may constitute illegal FX conversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration record issued via the delegated bank or SAFE portal, board and shareholder resolutions approving the capital injection, the overseas shareholder's corporate bank statement showing the exact remittance source, the remittance instruction with the correct BOP transaction purpose code for direct investment equity capital, a negative-list sector screening declaration, and the bank's capital contribution verification certificate at the time of conversion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service payments to related overseas entities, especially in low-tax jurisdictions, may trigger transfer-mis-pricing and tax evasion red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous transfer pricing master file and local file, an entity-level functional and economic substance analysis, employee and payroll evidence, subcontracting agreements, benchmark pricing studies, corporate income tax returns and VAT invoices, tax residency certificates of each related payee, and management representation letters signed under penalty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas shareholder must complete SAFE FDI registration through the designated bank or the local SAFE office before remitting. The wire must be sent from the shareholder's own overseas corporate bank account, never a client or third-party account. The remittance reference should state 'FDI capital injection' and use the balance-of-payments transaction code mapped by the receiving bank to the SAFE direct investment equity category for foreign-invested enterprises. Funds must be credited to the WFOE's Foreign Currency Capital Account. After receipt, the bank verifies the transaction against SAFE's capital item information system, completes the cross-border declaration, and can settle the funds into RMB under the capital account settlement policy for the entity's approved business purposes. Effective settlement use is limited to operating expenses, salaries, professional fees, software and infrastructure procurement; capital account RMB funds cannot be used for domestic equity investment or entrusted loans without specific SAFE approval. The bank then issues the capital contribution verification certificate needed for the positive enterprise credit information filing and any statutory audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outsourced CFO service expenses, vendor payments, software subscriptions, and professional fees, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 via the relationship bank, supported by the underlying service agreement, invoice, VAT or tax withholding certificate, and a valid SAFE service-transaction purpose code. For any incidental physical goods trade, a confirmed or unconfirmed commercial letter of credit issued under MT700 or a documentary collection under URC 522 is permissible, requiring original bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, inspection certificates, and proof of cargo movement. All disbursements must be matched to the WFOE's operating obligations, transfer pricing policy, and the documented economic substance of the transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/foreign currency forward contracts executed with an authorized Chinese bank against genuine current or capital account exposure, evidenced by underlying invoices, contracts, or loan documents.

RMB/foreign currency swap transactions for temporary capital account and current account working capital conversion, subject to maturity alignment with the underlying cash flow and SAFE documentation rules.

Foreign exchange option structures such as zero-premium collars or participating forwards to hedge service fee receivables or future dividend repatriation, provided the bank's product eligibility and risk acknowledgement requirements are satisfied.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the onshore WFOE; all hedging must be executed onshore through licensed commercial banks under SAFE's real-demand principle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Credit Information Report filed online through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local Market Regulation Administrations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 puts the entity on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations after a 10-working-day grace period; if abnormal status is not remedied within three consecutive years, the entity is moved to the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, subject to joint disciplinary restrictions and possible revocation of business license. Falsification or concealment of information carries an administrative fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 30,000; chronic non-publication is an administrative strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) jointly with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), submitted through the SAMR enterprise annual report portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for the prior calendar year; integrated with the general enterprise annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission, late filing, or incomplete foreign investment information leads to a rectification order; refusal to rectify is penalized with an administrative fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000, and false or misleading reporting may attract a fine up to RMB 200,000. Unreported equity or capital movements may be blocked for foreign exchange procedures, dividend remittances, and cross-border capital account filings until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 annually for the prior calendar year, with quarterly or monthly prepayment returns due within 15 days after each prescribed period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of RMB 2,000, or up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases, plus a daily overdue tax surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Underpaid tax caused by concealment or false returns is penalized at 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Persistent non-payment triggers enforced recovery, inclusion in the tax integrity blacklist, and denial of deregistration until all taxes and filings are cleared.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Related Party Transaction Report and Transfer Pricing Contemporaneous Documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax bureau, attached to the annual CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 annually, together with the corporate income tax annual settlement return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose related party arrangements or provide required transfer pricing documentation allows the tax authority to open a special tax adjustment investigation and impose interest on adjusted income; late or incomplete documentation also triggers administrative fines of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 and may shift the burden of proof to the taxpayer, increasing assessed income and tax liabilities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Audit by a PRC-licensed CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and board of directors; audited financial statements remain in the corporate statutory books and are produced to SAMR, MOFCOM, SAFE, STA, and other authorities upon lawful inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial report must be audited before shareholder approval, and in practice should be completed by May 31 to support the CIT annual settlement and the June 30 annual information report deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A WFOE without the compulsory CPA audit report violates the Company Law, Accounting Law, and foreign investment regulatory rules; regulators may issue correction orders, impose penalties on the company and responsible persons, and question dividends, capital reserves, and tax deductions reliant on unaudited financial statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption for a WFOE: PRC Company Law and Accounting Law require every company, including a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, to have its annual financial report audited each fiscal year by an independent accounting firm licensed in the People's Republic of China. Even a dormant WFOE with zero turnover and minimal assets is subject to the annual CPA audit. Quantitative triggers that tighten the audit regime include: (i) entities holding any financial-institution or money-services license must engage an annually renewed licensed CPA firm with additional regulatory reporting; (ii) public offering undertakings require review or audit on an interim schedule; and (iii) multinational groups with annual related-party transactions crossing the State Administration of Taxation local-file thresholds must support the audited statements with transfer pricing documentation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE, also referred to as Chinese GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS, supplemented by the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards for small taxpayers where eligibility applies; statutory ledgers and financial reports must be prepared in Chinese renminbi under the PRC accounting law, and multicurrency records are permitted only as auxiliary ledgers.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not operate a standalone annual UBO confirmation form for ordinary WFOEs; instead, beneficial ownership information must be registered with SAMR under the Beneficial Owner Information Administration Measures effective from November 1, 2024, at incorporation and within 30 calendar days after any change in beneficial ownership. A beneficial owner is any natural person who ultimately owns or controls the WFOE directly or indirectly, generally at or above the 25% shareholding, voting right, or control threshold, or who controls the entity through financial, personnel, or other arrangements. Separately, every annual enterprise credit information report captures current shareholders, contributed capital, equity changes, and control chain information, and any shareholding transfer or new equity pledge must be filed with SAMR and for foreign investment information purposes within 30 days after the corporate resolution or transfer agreement, with the register of members updated contemporaneously.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 2,500 per year for a compliant virtual/registered address or business-park agency arrangement; USD 3,000 - USD 10,000 per year for a physical office address in a tier-1 city
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 for a simple single-entity WFOE with low transaction volume and no intercompany balances; USD 7,000 - USD 18,000 for multicurrency bookkeeping, virtual CFO revenue flows, related-party balances, and transfer pricing documentation requiring a full CPA audit opinion

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Enterprise Income Tax rate under Article 4 of the EIT Law)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For qualifying Small and Low-Profit Enterprises, taxable income up to RMB 3 million is effectively taxed at 5% (reduced to 25% inclusion at the 20% statutory rate), available through 2027. Additional deduction for R&D expenses at 175% (or 200% for manufacturing) is available, but a virtual CFO consultancy typically does not qualify for high-tech enterprise treatment. No specific free-zone or patent box regime applies to this services scope unless the entity is established in a special pilot zone (e.g., Hainan, where a 15% rate may apply to encouraged industries).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (A-type)) and supporting schedules, filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration's E-Tax Portal (e-tax.chinatax.gov.cn or local provincial e-filing systems). Quarterly provisional returns (Form A200000 or similar) with annual consolidation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus quarterly (or monthly) provisional returns with annual reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 5 months after each calendar year-end (i.e., by May 31 of the following year). Quarterly provisional returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, and January 15 for Q4).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from the provision of virtual CFO and bookkeeping services, including fees billed through payment rails (Stripe, Wise).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue in CNY using the spot exchange rate at transaction date or the monthly average rate published by SAFE. Revenue from non-resident clients should still be fully taxable in China as the WFOE is a Chinese tax resident. Ensure no artificial deferral by parking revenue in offshore accounts; all worldwide income is subject to CICT and must be included in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs directly attributable to producing the revenue (e.g., subcontractor fees paid to third-party bookkeepers, software licensing for accounting tools).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service payments to related parties must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be supported by a proper service agreement and contemporaneous documentation; otherwise, such deductions may be challenged under transfer pricing adjustments. Any promotional discount or rebate received from a non-resident vendor must be booked as income or offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge levied on VAT paid for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These surcharges are deductible for CIT. Non-resident advisors should ensure that any late VAT penalties or interest are not deducted, as penalties and fines are non-deductible under the EIT Law. Confirm the correct VAT basis if cross-border service income was zero-rated or exempt under VAT rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, platform fees, and sales commissions incurred to obtain clients, including fees paid to digital marketplaces and referral agents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE engages a non-resident sales agent, the commission must be at arm's length and may trigger WHT on service fees paid to a non-resident without a permanent establishment in China (usually 10% on gross income). The WFOE must withhold and remit the tax and file the relevant withholding return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries of directors and staff, legal fees, rent, office expenses, and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident directors or service providers for management fees require DTA analysis and must be substantiated with contracts and proof of beneficial ownership; otherwise, they may be recharacterized as disguised dividends subject to 10% WHT. Ensure payroll for resident employees is properly registered and social insurance contributions are deducted only when actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank charges, foreign exchange losses, and interest on working-capital loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to 10% WHT (possibly reduced by treaty; e.g., 7% under China-Hong Kong DTA), and thin-capitalization rules limit deductible interest to a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio per CICT Article 46. A proof of loan purpose and fund usage must be retained to support the interest deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before tax, computed as operating profit plus non-operating income minus non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that any intercompany charges from the non-resident parent (e.g., group overhead allocations) have been properly documented under the arm's-length principle; undeclared benefits received from shareholders may be recharacterized as additional contribution or dividend, creating WHT exposure. Non-operating income such as government subsidies or compensation should be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back non-deductible items, applying transfer pricing adjustments, and subtracting prior-year losses within the 5-year carryforward limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the base for the 25% headline tax (or applicable preferential rate). The WFOE must maintain a complete reconciliation schedule; non-resident shareholders should expect the WFOE to compute this accurately to avoid under-withholding on future dividends. If the WFOE reports a loss for several consecutive years, tax authorities may trigger an economic substance audit and challenge the continuity of the business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of annual CIT return: administrative fine from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 if the tax authority orders a correction within a time limit and the taxpayer fails to comply (PRC Tax Administration and Collection Law, Art. 62). In addition, a late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax applies. If under-reporting taxable income is intentional and constitutes tax evasion, the taxpayer faces recovery of tax, a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded (Art. 63), and criminal liability for evasion if the amount evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable (Criminal Law Art. 201) – leading to imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines for the entity and its responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed to non-resident corporate shareholders, unless a lower rate is available under an applicable Double Tax Agreement/treaty (e.g., 5% for a Hong Kong resident company holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must be the 'beneficial owner' of the dividend and obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence. The WFOE as the withholding agent must submit on behalf of the non-resident an 'Information Report form for the Enjoyment of Tax Treaty Treatment' (Form 1202 in the E-tax system) before or at the time of withholding. The procedure follows the 'self-assessment, declaration for enjoyment, and document retention' mechanism under National Tax Administration Bulletin 2019 No. 35. The supporting documents (TRC, shareholding register, and substance evidence) must be retained for 10 years and be available for inspection on demand. If the beneficial ownership test is not met, treaty benefits are denied and the full 10% WHT becomes due, along with interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 10% for interest and royalties sourced in China paid to non-residents. Treaty rates may be reduced (e.g., 7% for interest under the China-Hong Kong DTA, 5% for royalties under the China-Singapore DTA; many treaties retain 10%). All payments must be reported via the withholding filing, and the payee must establish beneficial ownership to enjoy treaty relief. For royalties related to software or know-how, source taxation may apply if the use is in China; careful characterisation is needed between service income and royalty income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: annual related-party transactions of other types (including service fees) exceeding RMB 40 million (approx. USD 5.5 million) require preparation of a Local File. Master File: required when the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue exceeds RMB 5 billion (approx. USD 700 million) and the entity is part of the group. Thresholds per STA Bulletin No. 42 of 2016. Additionally, a Country-by-Country Report is triggered if the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion (approx. USD 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not impose an Economic Substance Regulations regime in the offshore sense, but the substance-over-form doctrine applies under the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and Article 26 of the EIT Law. For a WFOE with a virtual CFO business, the core income-generating activities (CIGA) – contracting, team management, billing, and accounting – must be performed in China with real personnel and decision-making substance. A shell WFOE that merely routes income to a related offshore entity without Chinese substance may be recharacterized, and treaty benefits may be denied for lack of beneficial ownership. Directors must ensure that the board meetings, books, and employment records reflect actual operations in China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE derives revenue from non-resident clients through Stripe/Wise but fails to record these overseas receipts, or intentionally parks funds in an offshore bank account and files a zero CIT return. This falsifies the books and hides taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration and Collection Law (TACL) and Article 201 of the Criminal Law. Administrative sanction: recovery of the unpaid tax plus a penalty of 50% to 5 times (500%) of the evaded tax. Where the evasion exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable, criminal liability arises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or instructed the concealment may be held personally liable for the civil restitution of the evaded tax and penalties. They also face a travel ban (blacklisting) preventing departure from China until tax liabilities are settled (Art. 44 TACL). Under Criminal Law Art. 201 and 211, the responsible director may be sentenced to up to 3 years imprisonment (or 3–7 years if the amount is huge) and criminal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Fraud – Fabricated Deductions / Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE creates fictitious service invoices from a related shell company (e.g., a Hong Kong or BVI entity) for 'management consulting' that was never performed, in order to reduce Chinese taxable income and remit funds abroad without dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Article 63 TACL (falsification of accounting vouchers) and may constitute 'fraudulent tax filing'. Sanctions include a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, disallowance of the deduction, and potential criminal exposure under Criminal Law Art. 201. If fictitious VAT special invoices are involved, criminal liability for issuing false invoices under Criminal Law Art. 205 may apply (for ordinary invoices, Art. 205-1).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced if the director used the WFOE as an instrument to commit fraud. Directors must restore the amount of tax avoided with personal assets. A court may impose an exit ban and freeze personal bank accounts. Criminal imprisonment of 3–7 years for tax evasion or up to 10 years for issuing false invoices may be imposed on the 'directly responsible supervisor and other directly responsible persons'.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse (Beneficial Ownership Failure)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is nominally owned by a Hong Kong or Mauritius holding company that has no employees, offices, or business activity; dividends are routed to the intermediate shell and then to the ultimate resident, while the WFOE and the shell claim a 5% low dividend rate under the DTA without substantive business activity in the treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates the General Anti-Abuse Rule under Article 47 EIT Law and the specific anti-treaty-shopping provisions in STA Annual Announcement 2009 No. 601 and Public Notice 2018 No. 9 (Beneficial Ownership). The tax authority may deny treaty benefits and re-characterize the dividend as fully taxable at 10% (or higher if no treaty), impose an additional 10% WHT difference plus a 50%–500% penalty for under-withholding, and assess interest on the shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly arranged the artificial structure are jointly liable for the corporate tax debts to the extent they participated in the abuse. They can be placed on a 'non-trustworthy taxpayer' list (黑名单), which triggers travel bans, restrictions on high consumption (e.g., air travel, luxurious hotels), and credit disabilities. Criminal charges for fraudulent tax refund or evasion may follow if the arrangement concealed taxable income. The corporate veil will be pierced to hold the directors personally responsible for the unpaid taxes and penalties.
